what: Act One is not a faster showreel. It is an audit that becomes a film: it reads the public site, keeps receipts, rejects what it cannot prove, makes three real directions, fails one, repairs it, and removes waiting.
why: The viewer sees proof before persuasion. Muted, it reads as a real site being inspected. With sound, it feels like evidence being logged: pin, measure, strike out. The thrill comes late, when the strict audit breaks into three distinct creative systems and then judges itself.

what: No bed at the start. Tap, page breath, underline drag, sample tick, measured ticks, muted strike-out. These sounds recur with the visual verbs. Music enters only when the system starts making choices, pivots to counted ticks on scoring, then thins for the final proof hold.
why: Courtroom restraint. Four shot classes only: full browser read, 130–160% evidence-close, 3-up verdict, near-full-frame proof. Every claim uses one of three verbs: pin, measure, strike out. The triptych is the single rupture where inspection becomes choice.

what: Opening with “This is the brief.”
why: Tempting and strategically right, but too writerly for the first breath. The image can prove it faster. We spend those seconds on visible extraction and refusal instead. (proposed by story)

what: A 10–12 second near-still opening inspection.
why: The severity is right, but not the duration. By six seconds the viewer must see concrete verbs on the live site, not just restraint. (proposed by art)

what: Ending with the finished film back inside the live page.
why: It closes the loop neatly, but miniaturises the result when we need inspectable scale. Cost: we lose the clever “site in, film out” visual rhyme. (proposed by product)

what: A separate collapsing timeline graphic.
why: Too familiar for a speed claim. The calendar argument must happen over the finished render, and only empty waiting may disappear. (proposed by motion)

what: Triptych as the only invention.
why: One rupture is a gimmick if the rest stays templated. The recurring pin/measure/strike grammar now carries the whole film. (proposed by art)

what: Scoring all three lanes with lots of overlays.
why: That would read as software garnish. We compare three systems, then isolate one named failure and repair it visibly. (proposed by contrarian)
